data.description: Found by the BC-17 cycle-2 review (art_01M4WJJ802GNNSTN174BB1MX2R). On a Linux daemon without Docker Desktop's uid mapping, make up creates $root/frontend/node_modules (the web service's anonymous-volume mount point) and the api writes $root/data/listings.db as root inside the bind mounts. scripts/verify-dist.sh then runs npm ci natively (EACCES, make check fails) and cannot rm -rf the temp dir. Not reproduced on macOS (all runs clean). Root cause is compose.yaml (BC-13 design), not BC-17. Options: compose user: for the services, or a documented Linux caveat in the verify-dist header and README.
data.title: verify-dist on a Linux Docker host: root-owned bind-mount paths break native make check and temp cleanup

provenance.reason: Out of scope for BC-17 (macOS host, inherited Compose design)

data.body: From the BC-17 cycle-4 review (art on BC-17, HEAD 70fa0e0): scripts/verify-dist.sh runs make check after make up (verify-dist.sh:384,438), so on a Linux Engine host its own make check hits the root-owned frontend/node_modules mount point (npm ci EACCES); rm -rf cleanup still succeeds because the parents are user-owned. Fold into this ticket's fix: either run make check before make up in verify-dist, or state the macOS-only expectation in its header. README.md now carries the Linux note (Orchestrator decision 06:50Z).
